system_info.name: ArthikAI
system_info.mission: Empowering individuals and families with low or irregular income through practical budgeting, emergency savings, and public support awareness.
system_info.disclaimer: ⚠️ Disclaimer: ArthikAI provides general financial literacy and public resource information for educational purposes. It does not provide certified financial, legal, or investment advice.

emergency_fund_limited_income.title: 4-Step Practical Emergency Fund Plan for Limited Income

steps.name: Establish a Micro-Target First
steps.description: Don't get overwhelmed by conventional '6 months of expenses' advice. Start with a realistic micro-target of ₹1,000 to ₹3,000 (enough to cover a sudden clinic visit, cycle repair, or emergency grocery refill).

steps.name: Audit & Plug Hidden Leaks
steps.description: Track every ₹10-₹20 expense for 7 days. Look for recurring daily drains (impulse snacks, unnecessary mobile recharges, ATM transaction fees). Redirecting just ₹30/day saves ₹900/month.

steps.name: Separate from Everyday Spending
steps.description: Never keep your emergency buffer in the same cash pocket or primary spending account. Use a dedicated zero-balance account (like PM Jan Dhan) or a physical lockbox to prevent impulse spending.

steps.name: The Daily Micro-Deposit Habit
steps.description: Treat your emergency fund like a mandatory daily utility bill. Save ₹20 - ₹50 at the end of every working day before spending on non-essentials. Within 3-4 months, you will have a sturdy ₹3,000 - ₹5,000 shock absorber.

low_income_budgeting_rule.name: 70 / 20 / 10 Survival-to-Security Budget
low_income_budgeting_rule.description: Standard 50/30/20 budgets are unrealistic for low-income households where essentials consume the majority of earnings. The 70/20/10 structure is purpose-built for tight budgets.

essentials_needs.items: Rent, groceries/ration, essential utilities, medicines, children's school fees, basic transport.

debt_relief_and_savings.items: Urgent debt repayment (clearing high-interest loans first) + micro-emergency fund building.

discretionary_buffer.items: Small personal comforts, unavoidable social obligations, minor festival treats without taking fresh debt.

public_schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)
public_schemes.benefit: Zero-balance savings account, free RuPay debit card with ₹2 Lakh accidental insurance cover, and overdraft facility up to ₹10,000 after 6 months.
public_schemes.eligibility: Any Indian citizen aged 10+ without a basic bank account. Requires minimal KYC (Aadhaar or voter card).

public_schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)
public_schemes.benefit: Accidental death and full disability cover of ₹2 Lakh for just ₹20 per YEAR.
public_schemes.eligibility: Ages 18 to 70 with an active bank account.

public_schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
public_schemes.benefit: Life insurance cover of ₹2 Lakh on death due to any reason for ₹436 per YEAR.
public_schemes.eligibility: Ages 18 to 50 with a bank account.

public_schemes.name: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
public_schemes.benefit: Guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 after age 60 for unorganized sector workers.
public_schemes.eligibility: Ages 18 to 40. Monthly contribution depends on entry age (e.g. ₹42 to ₹210/month at age 18).

public_schemes.name: PM MUDRA Yojana (Shishu Loans)
public_schemes.benefit: Collateral-free loans up to ₹50,000 for small vendors, artisans, kirana stores, and self-employed micro-entrepreneurs at low institutional interest rates.
public_schemes.eligibility: Small business owners, micro-entrepreneurs, street vendors.

public_schemes.name: PM SVANidhi
public_schemes.benefit: Working capital collateral-free loan of ₹10,000 (escalating to ₹20,000 and ₹50,000 on timely repayment) with 7% interest subsidy and cashback on digital transactions.

public_schemes.name: National Food Security / Antyodaya Anna Yojana (PDS)
public_schemes.benefit: Highly subsidized/free foodgrains (wheat, rice, coarse grains) through ration shops under One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC).
public_schemes.eligibility: Priority households and poorest families identified by state governments.

moneylender_crisis: Stop borrowing from unorganized local moneylenders charging 5% to 10% per MONTH (60-120% per year).
Approach nationalized bank branches or regional rural banks (RRBs) for Mudra or self-help group (SHG) micro-loans at 9-12% annual rate.
Join or form a local Self Help Group (SHG) under NRLM (National Rural Livelihoods Mission) to access low-interest community credit pools.
Prioritize high-interest loans first ('Avalanche method') to stop compounding interest from draining your monthly cash.

guardrail_refusals.speculative_crypto_stocks: I cannot provide stock market picks, cryptocurrency speculation, or trading advice. My role as an SDG 1 Financial Inclusion Assistant is to help you build financial security through safe budgeting, emergency funds, debt reduction, and government welfare resources. Let's focus on securing your emergency reserve first.
guardrail_refusals.get_rich_quick: Please beware of schemes promising doubled money or guaranteed 20%+ monthly returns—these are illegal pyramid or chit fund scams. Real financial freedom comes from steady micro-savings, protected bank accounts, and debt control.
